title: Build a Loading and Saving Program

blocks.text: A Complete Program Starts with Verifiable Requirements

An inspection station receives counts by group and needs to load them, produce a report, and save the data for later recovery. Build the complete program from these requirements. You may consult earlier lessons, but the initial editor provides neither the models nor the bodies of the readers, composer, or comparison.

Use the previously defined Conjunto format: red, green, and blue groups, each present at most once; records with IDs 0..9 unique within their group; quantities from 0..10. Preserve both vectors' order, empty groups, and zero-valued records. The complete sample must have an outer closing marker and only whitespace up to EOF.

During one execution, create inspecciones_entrada.txt containing { set { group red 7[0;0] 2[3;1] } { group blue } }. Check opening, writing, and closing before reopening it for reading. Initialize the previous state with green and 9[6;2]. If the sample is invalid, preserve that state and finish without opening inspecciones_salida.txt. Report a reading failure as a technical problem, not as a valid sample.

If the sample is valid, replace the entire state, compose its text before opening inspecciones_salida.txt, write it, and check closing the output. Reopen the file during the same execution, read it, and compare all its data with the loaded state. Calculate the quantity report from the records; do not substitute it for that comparison.
Design Responsibilities and Cases Before Coding

Choose functions and contracts. Separate character interpretation, data validity, acceptance of the complete set, text composition, file operations, and reporting. Readers and composers protect their destination objects on false; neither promises to restore consumed characters or a file whose writing failed.

blocks.question: The first group is read successfully, but the set's closing marker is missing. When should the output file be opened?
options: After the first group, because some data can already be saved.
After the reader fails, to write only the provisional data.
It must not be opened: no complete sample was accepted.
blocks.explanation: The program generates output data only after accepting the sample and composing its entire text.

blocks.text: Prepare cases distinguishing the policies: the base sample, an empty set, an empty red group, the same local ID in red and blue, a repeated empty group, a repeated record, quantity 11, a truncated second group, and text after the outer closing marker. Predict the final state and report in each case before coding.

The maximum total for either quantity is 3 groups × 10 records × 10 units = 300. Justify this bound before summing into int. If you change the data domain, revisit the bound; validating the format alone does not prove every later calculation safe.
Build Independently from an Empty Editor

Write the types, functions, and main. The accepted base sample must produce five lines: Input accepted; Groups: 2; Accepted: 3; Rejected: 1; Verification: 1. Use the exact labels and a line break between lines. For rejected data, show two lines: Input rejected and State preserved: 1. A technical error needs a message identifying its stage and exit code 1. Both a valid run and a data rejection exit with code 0.

Check every result before using it. An input stream that normally reaches EOF is not treated as though bad() indicated a failure. Do not clear state flags during parsing to accept incomplete data. Local ifstream objects can close at the end of their scope; explicitly check writing and close() for each ofstream, because finishing character insertion does not prove that closing succeeded.

The reference is on the next page. This lab creates its own samples with relative paths during execution; it does not import user files. Write and reread in the same run: the exercise does not rely on those files remaining available afterward and does not export documents.
Later Reference: One Possible Complete Solution

The reference produces the five agreed lines and the data file { set { group red 7[0;0] 2[3;1] } { group blue } }. The empty blue group remains present and the zero-valued record is not discarded. Text is composed before opening the output file; writing and closing are checked before reading it again.

The reader's bool determines acceptance; bad() distinguishes a reading failure. The ifstream objects are scoped to their blocks. We do not clear an invalid extraction to pretend it ended correctly, nor do we use quantities from the previous state after a valid read has replaced it.
Test Rejection, Empty Input, and Actual Preservation

Run again, changing only the sample string to { set }. Expect Input accepted, Groups: 0, Accepted: 0, Rejected: 0, and Verification: 1. Then test { set { group red } }: that group counts as present even when both totals remain zero.

In separate tests, remove the outer closing marker, add a repeated empty group, and change a quantity to 11. Each case must produce Input rejected and State preserved: 1. Check the previous group ID, record ID, and both quantities, not just the collection size. The output data file must not be opened on this rejection path.

As a preservation experiment, first create an output file containing MARKER during your own test, before presenting an invalid sample. After rejection, reopen that file and check that MARKER is still present. This distinguishes not opening the output from opening it with truncation. Your program creates the marker file during execution.

blocks.question: The invalid sample preserved MARKER because the output was never opened. What can you conclude?
options: That the rejection path avoids modifying the file; it does not prove restoration after a failed write.
That any power cut during a valid write always preserves MARKER.
That close() may be omitted if there was a previous marker.
blocks.explanation: This tests one specific control-flow path. A later write might truncate or partially fail and requires a different guarantee.

blocks.text: Now distinguish data rejection from an opening failure. In another run, keep the valid base sample and change only the saving path to inspecciones_entrada.txt/inspecciones_salida.txt. The program already created and closed inspecciones_entrada.txt as a regular file, so it cannot use it as a directory. Before running, predict the message, return code, and files that should exist. Expect Output open error, exit code 1, and the original input unchanged, without creating a new output file. Do not expect Input rejected: the set was already accepted. Use only test files created during the run. This checks opening, not recovery from partial writes or failure on close.

Build two small tests independent of the parser. In the first, open ensayo_escritura.txt and check opening; close it successfully and verify the first close; then attempt to write TEST. Observe !escritura immediately after insertion, before any further close(), to attribute failure to the operation that caused it. In the second, open ensayo_cierre.txt, write TEST and check writing; close it and verify that first close; call close() a second time, then observe !cierre. Predict each stream's state and each file's contents separately.

Build both tests from the minimal editor. Reopen their files with ifstream during the same execution and inspect the saved contents. Display two lines: Write: B;Empty: B and Close: B;Preserved: B, each B being the observed bool as 0 or 1; Preserved compares the recovered text with TEST. Check earlier stages before proceeding. A failed opening does not establish the write experiment. EOF of an empty file is expected; bad() still identifies a separate problem. Do not clear flags to pretend to write through a closed connection.

These files are private samples of the current execution. The tests deliberately trigger defined stream-use errors; they do not simulate a damaged disk or demonstrate recovery from a partial write. The reference follows your attempt on page 7.
Review and Transfer Without Silently Changing the Contract

Review criteria: clear responsibilities; no data used before successful extraction; validation of every identity; previous state unchanged on rejection; fresh candidates; a readable data format; preserved order and presence; output not opened for invalid data; opening, writing, and closing checked; and complete round-trip comparison. Messages must distinguish data rejection from file errors.

Review: rebuild a small function without consulting its reference, such as name conversion, duplicate detection, record comparison, or summing a report. Use it in your program and repeat a case that might expose an error. Ensure the change does not weaken guarantees in the other stages.

Transfer: replace the totals report with one identifying the group with the largest total of accepted quantities. Before coding, specify what happens for an empty set, ties, and groups present but empty. Keep the data format and round-trip comparison unchanged; a different report does not authorize removing data from the file.

The primary source discusses reading and representing data (Stroustrup, 2024, sections 9.5–9.9, pp. 264–275). This practice integrates concepts from chapters 0–9. The problem, requirements, program, and tests are original to this learning path.
Distinguish Write Failure from a Second Close

Expect Write: 1;Empty: 1 and Close: 1;Preserved: 1 on separate lines. In the first test, opening and the first close succeed: failure appears when writing through the closed stream, and TEST is not written. In the second test, writing and the first close succeed, saving TEST; the failure appears on the second close(). A stream in a failed state at the end does not imply that its file is empty.

The first getline reaches EOF without extracting characters because the file is empty. Here we therefore check EOF, absence of bad(), and the recovered text; do not treat this as successfully reading a line. The second test must recover TEST and check the end. On any other read problem, the reference exits with code 1 and does not attribute the result to the planned experiment.

Return to the complete program and separate its stages similarly: check after writing, check after closing, and identify the stage where failure occurred. Keep invalid sample rejection on another path. Do not open the output data file before the input is accepted and its complete text composed.
Transfer the Report: Sum by Group and Preserve the Data

Review the transfer task: the winning group has the largest SUM of accepted quantities among all its records. Do not compare just the largest individual record or add rejected quantities. A group has at most ten records and each accepted quantity is 0..10, so its sum is 0..100 and fits in int. The set must already be valid before selection.

Set the tie policy: if several groups have the same total, the one appearing first in the groups vector wins, because it preserves input order. A present group without records totals zero and participates in comparisons; a group whose records have zero accepted quantities also participates. With no groups, there is no winner. Do not confuse absence with a total of zero, or input order with alphabetic or group-ID order.

Build seleccionar_mayor(const Conjunto& conjunto), returning the Informe_mayor declared in the editor without printing or modifying data. If a group exists, return hay_grupo=true, its ID, and the total of its accepted quantities. With no groups, return hay_grupo=false, id=-1, and aceptados=0. The editor provides models, readers, composer, comparison, and the known file stages, but neither selection's body nor report presentation. Define the function outside main.

Complete main to show six lines for valid data: Input accepted; Groups: N; Top group: name; Group accepted: N; Data preserved: 1; Verification: 1. Include a space after each label that has a value. With no groups, show Top group: none and Group accepted: 0. Before and after getting the report, compare a full data copy and the composed texts; comparison must cover groups, records, both quantities, and both orders. Keep the complete comparison with the data reread from the file. On a technical error or failed comparison, report the stage and exit with code 1 as in the earlier program.

The editor starts with green and 2[5;1], red with 4[3;0] and 8[3;2], and empty blue. First work out the winning group and total: the largest individual record does not determine the group sum. Test { set } and { set { group green } } too; predict how their Top group and Group accepted lines distinguish absence from an empty group that is present.

For ties, use { set { group green 8[4;0] } { group red 1[4;3] } { group blue 0[1;0] } }, then swap only the positions of green and red. For zero totals, use { set { group blue } { group green 7[0;2] } { group red 1[0;0] } }. Include an empty group before another with a positive total, and a group containing ten records of ten accepted units. Predict the winner and total for each run before observing them, and require Data preserved: 1 and Verification: 1. Empty groups, zero-valued records, and order must remain in the file even if they do not change report totals.

Compare your work with every case before consulting the reference. The editor does not grade the report automatically. Equivalent implementations preserving the interface, domain, ties, and data are valid; do not hardcode outputs for particular input texts.
A Later Reference for Comparing the Selection

This reference uses different data: red with 6[4;2], green with 8[3;1] and 1[3;0], and empty blue. Green totals six, exceeding red's four. Expect Input accepted, Groups: 3, Top group: green, Group accepted: 6, Data preserved: 1, and Verification: 1, one label per line. Record order 8 then 1 and the empty blue group remain in the saved data.

hay_grupo distinguishes no winner from a present group whose sum is zero. The first group may be selected even when it has no records. Later, the reference replaces the result only for a strictly greater total; equal totals keep the previous group, hence the earliest in input order. Other implementations are valid if they follow this contract.

The copy antes_del_informe preserves all values and their order before inspection. mismos_datos compares the complete data, and a second composition checks that the report has not changed its text. Comparison with recuperado also maintains the file round trip. The correct winner, an equal size, or an equal sum is not a substitute for those checks. The program checks insertion and close() separately, as in the earlier tests.
Review Ties, Presence, and Preservation with Other Data

blocks.question: Predict the six lines of this report. Preserve input order when applying the tie rule.
answers:
Input accepted
Groups: 3
Top group: green
Group accepted: 5
Data preserved: 1
Verification: 1
blocks.explanation: Green totals 2+3=5, and red totals five. Green appears first and wins the tie; empty blue totals zero. The report changes neither data nor order, and the complete round-trip comparison remains true.

blocks.question: Predict the six lines when a group with no records precedes two groups whose accepted quantities are zero.
answers:
Input accepted
Groups: 3
Top group: blue
Group accepted: 0
Data preserved: 1
Verification: 1
blocks.explanation: All three groups are present and their sums are zero. Blue is first and is a valid winner even though empty; the label none is not displayed. Red and green records, with both quantities, remain in the set and in the file.

blocks.question: A variant moves the winning group to the beginning of the vector before saving. All values and the correct winner are preserved. Does this meet the report contract?
options: Yes: the winner's name and total are the only required results.
No: group order also belongs to the data.
Yes, provided each group retains its records and both quantities.
blocks.explanation: Inspection may not reorder the set. Saving and rereading an already reordered set can produce equality between those states; comparison with the copy made before reporting detects the loss of original order.

blocks.text: The preservation test checks identities, both quantities, empty but present groups, and both orders, as well as the composed text. Selection and file verification have separate responsibilities: choosing the correct largest total does not prove the data were preserved. Keep these cases alongside opening, writing, and closing tests, without turning technical errors into data rejection.
